result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-022.md in full, then read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's ACTUAL current code line-by-line (lines 109-248 for registerForEvent, 314-436 for the new withdraw logic), per this task's extra-scrutiny instruction since this run modifies REQ-020's atomic-capacity function. registerForEvent surgical-modification check (line-by-line against design §3): decideRegistrationOutcome (lines 48-74) is byte-for-byte unchanged -- confirmed by reading every line, zero diff inside that function. The events-row `FOR UPDATE` lock acquisition (lines 117-129) is unmoved, same query shape as before. Transaction structure (one db.transaction wrapping the whole function) is unchanged. The ONLY changes are: (a) line 140's existing-row SELECT now also selects `id` alongside `admission` (was admission-only before); (b) lines 145-154 compute `existingAdmission` (raw 'withdrawn' normalized to null before being passed into decideRegistrationOutcome -- the function itself never sees a raw 'withdrawn' value) and `existingRegistrationId` (non-null only when raw admission was 'withdrawn'); (c) step 8's write (lines 195-219) branches UPDATE-vs-INSERT on `existingRegistrationId`, with the UPDATE's SET clause naming only admission/source/qr_token (never id, never created_at, confirmed by reading the object literal at lines 199-203). admittedCount computation (lines 157-164) and its query are untouched -- the count query selects rows by eventId+admission='admitted' exactly as before, with no interaction with the new existingRegistrationId logic. This is exactly as surgical as designed -- no additional surface changed. NEW concurrency scenario, independently constructed and run (not copied from BACKEND-DEV): wrote a throwaway test file apps/bot/src/domain/reviewer-scratch-withdraw-race.db.test.ts (deleted immediately after use -- git status --porcelain confirmed clean before continuing) with two scenarios against the already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, port 55432): (1) 50 iterations, capacity=1 event: userA is registered and admitted sequentially, then userA's withdrawRegistration and userB's registerForEvent race via Promise.all for the same event. Result: PASS all 50 -- withdrawOutcome is always {kind:'withdrawn'}, userB's outcome is always 'admitted' or 'waitlisted' (never anything else), and a direct DB re-count after every iteration confirms admittedRows.length <= 1 always (never over capacity). Across the 50 iterations the race genuinely resolved both ways (B admitted 1/50, waitlisted 49/50 -- confirming this is a real race with both outcomes possible, not one side deterministically starving the other, and also confirming no double-admission occurred on the 1 iteration where B did land admitted). (2) 20 iterations, 5-way contention: a third caller (userC, already admitted) withdraws concurrently with two fresh registerForEvent calls (userD, userE) racing for the same capacity-1 seat. Result: PASS all 20 -- withdrawOutcome always 'withdrawn', admittedRows.length always <= 1, and never more than one of {D,E} admitted. Mechanism verified by reading the code, not just observed empirically: withdrawRegistration takes a FOR UPDATE lock on the registrations row only (never the events row), so it runs fully independently of registerForEvent's events-row lock; registerForEvent's admittedCount read is a plain (non-locking) SELECT taken under the events-row lock, so under Postgres READ COMMITTED it sees whichever side's write already committed at read time -- either way is a legitimate, non-overlapping outcome, and the events-row lock still fully serializes concurrent registerForEvent calls against each other (unchanged from REQ-020), which is the actual guarantee against over-admission. This confirms the withdraw modification did not reopen or introduce a capacity race. RE-RAN REQ-020's own concurrency test myself (not just trusted BACKEND-DEV's report): `TEST_DATABASE_URL=... npx vitest run apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts --reporter=verbose` -- the pre-existing 20-iteration/2-caller atomic-capacity test passed, exactly one of two concurrent registerForEvent calls admitted per iteration in all 20, matching baseline. Combined with my own new 50-iteration and 20-iteration (5-way) scenarios above, this constitutes independent re-derivation at a higher combined iteration count and under a materially different configuration (mixed register+withdraw contention) than BACKEND-DEV's own re-run, per this task's explicit instruction. AC1-AC5 independently re-verified by reading the actual test code and the domain/handler implementation (not just trusting the report): AC1 (apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts, 4 cases) -- /withdraw shows the two-button prompt only for an eligible registration (confirmButton/cancelButton callback_data match /^withdraw:(confirm|cancel):.+$/); tapping cancel produces methods=[answerCallbackQuery,sendMessage] with ZERO domain-module calls (confirmed by reading handlers/withdraw.ts's makeWithdrawCancelCallbackHandler, lines 158-166 -- it never imports or calls withdrawRegistration/decideWithdrawOutcome), row re-read confirms admission unchanged and zero audit rows; tapping confirm flips admission and writes exactly one audit row; a not-found registration is refused immediately with reply_markup undefined (no prompt at all). AC2 (registration.db.test.ts) -- read the dedicated case: admitted->withdrawn flips the admission column only, admittedCount (computeSeatsLeft's input) drops 1->0 on the very next read with zero code change to computeSeatsLeft, a subsequent registrant is then admitted. AC3 -- read the dedicated case: a direct-SQL checked_in_at flip (no check-in feature built yet, same discipline REQ-021 used) is refused with {kind:'checked-in'}, row re-read confirms admission still 'admitted'. AC4 -- read both dedicated cases line-by-line (lines 694-763): same registrationId (line 722, 759) AND same createdAt via toEqual (line 733, 762) survive a withdraw-then-reregister cycle, confirmed for both the admitted-capacity case and the still-full-waitlist case (proving §3.2's original-waitlist-position-preserved claim); a direct COUNT (line 725-729) confirms exactly one row for (event_id,user_id) throughout -- never a second INSERT. AC5 -- read the dedicated cases: exactly one audit_log row with action='registration.withdraw' on success (line 787), zero additional rows on a second withdrawal attempt against an already-withdrawn row (line 803-807, correctly returning {kind:'not-eligible',admission:'withdrawn'} with no write). Confirm/cancel UX cannot be bypassed with a forged/stale callback: read handlers/withdraw.ts's makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler (lines 101-154) -- it calls withdrawRegistration (the single authoritative check-and-write, §2.2) fresh at confirm time; it does NOT reuse anything from the earlier /withdraw display read. withdrawRegistration itself (registration.ts lines 348-401) re-derives ownership (`row.userId` compared against `actingUserId` fresh, line 374), eligibility, and checked-in status entirely from a fresh `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (lines 357-367) taken inside its own transaction -- never from any value the handler or the earlier /withdraw command supplied. A forged callback_data carrying someone else's registrationId is refused as 'not-owner' (decideWithdrawOutcome row 2) and mapped to the same generic refusedNotFound string as an actual not-found case (line 138-142), matching the non-disclosure discipline checkin.ts already established -- confirmed by reading decideWithdrawOutcome's pure-function test at registration.db.test.ts line 555-564 ('returns not-owner when the acting user does not own the row'). TOCTOU (checked-in during the confirmation window): confirmed by design and code that this is closed structurally, not just by convention. §2.3 states the checked_in_at read must happen fresh inside withdrawRegistration's own transaction, never reused from whatever populated the confirmation prompt -- and the code matches: getRegistrationForEventAndUser (the display-only read backing the /withdraw prompt, lines 412-436) is a completely separate, unlocked SELECT from withdrawRegistration's own FOR UPDATE read (lines 357-367); the confirm callback handler never threads any field from the earlier display read into withdrawRegistration -- it passes only registrationId (parsed fresh from callback_data) and actingUserId (re-resolved fresh via resolveActingUser at line 120). So a person shown the confirmation prompt while not checked in, who then gets checked in during the window, then taps confirm, is refused: withdrawRegistration's own fresh row-lock read at confirm time will see the now-non-null checked_in_at and decideWithdrawOutcome's row 3 fires. This exact mechanism (a direct-SQL checked_in_at flip between an initial read and a later withdrawRegistration call) is precisely what registration.db.test.ts's AC3 case already exercises end-to-end (register, then flip checked_in_at directly via raw SQL -- simulating a check-in that happened after any earlier display read -- then call withdrawRegistration and confirm refusal), which is a faithful proxy for the handler-level TOCTOU window even though no single test drives it through bot.handleUpdate() twice with a check-in event injected in between (there is no check-in feature/table trigger to inject one through yet, same scope boundary REQ-021's own test used the identical direct-SQL workaround for). No gap found in the actual guarantee; the coverage proxy is adequate. Audit-log count (AC5): confirmed by construction -- withdrawRegistration has exactly one writeAuditLog call (line 390-397), reached only on the single 'withdrawn'-returning branch, inside the same transaction as the one UPDATE (line 387). Test-confirmed as above. Domain logic outside handler bodies (decisions/0004): read handlers/withdraw.ts in full (167 lines) -- every domain decision (decideWithdrawOutcome, withdrawRegistration, getRegistrationForEventAndUser) is imported from domain/registration.ts and called, never reimplemented inline. The handler's own logic is limited to: argument parsing, i18n catalog lookups, InlineKeyboard construction, and a switch over outcome.kind to select which pre-existing catalog string to reply with -- no admission-state, ownership, or eligibility rule is evaluated in the handler body itself (the handler's own pre-check at §4.1 step 5 calls the SAME pure decideWithdrawOutcome function from the domain module, not a re-derived condition). No grammY import anywhere in domain/registration.ts (confirmed by reading its full import list, line 1-6). Compliant. now()/current_timestamp check (decisions/0006): grepped registration.ts case-insensitively -- only the file's own header comment (line 12) states the negative constraint; no actual SQL now()/current_timestamp call in the diff. withdrawRegistration's `at` parameter is used solely for the writeAuditLog call (line 396, an audit/bookkeeping write this rule explicitly exempts) -- decideWithdrawOutcome itself has no time-dependent predicate at all (checkedInAt is only ever compared to null, never to a clock value), so this function was never a candidate for the rule's violation in the first place, but I checked anyway rather than assuming. Compliant. Schema/migration review (decisions/0005, S13): confirmed `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/migrations` is empty and no schema.ts change appears in the diff -- REQ-022.md's own §0 no-schema-change claim (admission enum's 'withdrawn' member, checked_in_at, created_at, id, uq_registrations_event_user all pre-existed from REQ-011) independently re-confirmed against the current schema.ts. Not applicable this run -- no SECURITY-REVIEWER migration sign-off needed. Workspace/build-output check: no new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output directory moved -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (only existing files under apps/bot/src, i18n, docs, handoffs changed; no package.json touched). No scratch `docker build` required per my role file's trigger condition. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (all from repo root): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, unchanged). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (apps/web Next.js build succeeded, apps/bot's tsc -p tsconfig.json clean). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` -> 17 files / 196 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly, independently re-run by me against the same already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, migrated fresh by me via `npx drizzle-kit migrate` before running), not copied. Scope check: diff touches exactly the files the design named (domain/registration.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts, i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts, index.ts, plus the two test files, plus the design/handoff bookkeeping files) and nothing else. No scope creep found. No stray file left in the project root or elsewhere -- confirmed `git status --porcelain` clean after deleting my own scratch test file.

result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- mandatory, and pay particular attention given the capacity-function modification per this task's own instruction. My own assessment: this diff's registerForEvent modification touches the atomic-capacity guarantee's read path (an existing-row lookup gaining an `id` column and a conditional UPDATE-vs-INSERT branch) but not its locking discipline (the events-row FOR UPDATE lock is unmoved, confirmed above) or its outcome-decision function (decideRegistrationOutcome is byte-for-byte unchanged). The new withdrawRegistration function introduces a second, independent row-lock (on registrations, not events) and one new audit action (registration.withdraw) against an already-existing table/column set -- no new PII field, no new auth surface beyond the existing resolveActingUser gate, and ownership is checked (not-owner refusal) before any write. SECURITY-REVIEWER should still independently confirm this rather than take my assessment as sufficient, per this pipeline's own re-derive rule -- and should specifically re-examine the two-lock (events-row vs registrations-row) interaction I traced above, since that is the one genuinely new structural element this run adds to REQ-020's capacity guarantee.
